7dtn4:539: The essence of "Vibe Coding" is using natural language to blur the boundary between requirements and implementation. This has enormous value in the exploratory and prototyping phases, but when a system enters the stages of legacy maintenance and complex requirements, this ambiguity itself becomes the risk. The proposal of Harness Engineering and SDD essentially argues: AI-assisted development needs a structured "Deterministic Load-Bearing Layer" rather than pushing all decisions onto the model's stochastic generation capability. The article's judgment that "Vibe Coding carries very high risk for legacy applications" reveals a neglected engineering reality: for legacy systems with substantial business logic, boundary conditions, and exception handling, AI involvement must be extremely cautious. In a 50,000-line legacy system, the number of "implicit rules" far exceeds the explicit code. Any AI-generated code not filtered by a Harness may conflict with these implicit rules, resulting in systematic, hard-to-trace regression bugs. The relationship between SDD (Specification-Driven Development) and Harness Engineering deserves deeper examination: SDD provides the transformation layer from requirements to specifications (PRD → Design Knowledge Base), while Harness Engineering provides the governance layer from specifications to code (Design Knowledge Base → AI Execution). Together, they form a complete chain from business requirements to AI-generated outcomes.
